idiom_name: generator or closure bounce loop instead of recursive calls, with sys.setrecursionlimit as the ceiling
implementation_notes: CPython refuses tail-call elimination on purpose: the interpreter enforces sys.getrecursionlimit() and raises RecursionError rather than growing the C stack without bound. The idiomatic replacement is a driver loop that bounces between zero-argument callables (or generator steps pulled by the driver), with the mutually recursive functions returning the next step as a lambda instead of calling each other. This keeps the interpreter stack flat and needs no third-party library. Keep plain recursion where the depth is bounded by the data model; the driver is for data-driven or adversarial depth, and sys.setrecursionlimit is not an alternative because it raises the ceiling for the Python frame stack, not the C stack that actually overflows.
pitfalls: sys.setrecursionlimit only changes when the interpreter raises; a very large limit can crash the process with a C-stack overflow instead of a catchable RecursionError.
Anything callable satisfies the driver, so a step whose payload is callable is ambiguous - tag the step (for example a (kind, payload) tuple) when it matters.
A closure step keeps its captured arguments alive until it runs, so deep chains hold their intermediate objects; measure memory, not just call depth.
